Subject Wilhelm WLOCH, German Communist.

Made by D. S. Pitts. Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清：手写签名〕**

According to information received from the State Secret
Police, Berlin (German Scotland Yard, Special Branch), Wilhelm
WLOCH, who forms the subject of our file D. 7009, is now in
either Denmark or the United Kingdom. This person is in
possession of German P/port No. 47 issued at Berlin on May
12, 1932, which bears an endorsement that it is not to be
renewed or another document issued without permission having
been first obtained from the Police Department in Berlin.

From the same source it is learned that Wloch's wife
is Erna WLOCH nee FALKENBERG, who was born on December 18,
1896 in Berlin. She is in possession of German P/port No.
179/29 issued at Berlin on August 8, 1929.

WLOCH is known to the German home authorities as having
been a leading spirit in the German Communist Party from
1925 until 1933, when he fled the country.

Subject (in full) Wilhelm Wloch

Made by D.P.S. Henchman Forwarded by D.I.J. Coyne

With reference to the attached communication I have to
state that the present whereabouts of Wilhelm Wloch are
unknown. Following Wloch's departure from Shanghai on
10th November 1935 he is believed to have visited Hangchow;
it is said that he remained there for a few weeks and then
left China and went to Japan.

There is no confirmation of the rumour that he went to
Japan, but that this was the case is believed to be true by
his business associates and acquaintances.

Enquiries regarding Wloch instituted in Japan by the
Japanese Consular Authorities have proved negative in result.

Date January 17, 1936.
Subject Wloch, departure from Shanghai.
Made by D.P.S. Henchman Forwarded by S.B.Rm S//

Further to my report of 21st October 1935, I have to
state that Wilhelm Wloch left his address at 365 Route
Cardinal Mercier on 10th November 1935 and, it is believed,
proceeded to Hangchow. He left no forwarding address for
mail and did not signify that he had any intention of
returning to Shanghai. He has severed his connection with
the First Dental Clinic at 542 Avenue Joffre and is reported
to have lost a considerable sum of money in the business.
Further information concerning the period during which
Wloch resided in Europe has come to light: it is reported
that he was born in Berlin on 13th February 1897 and that
he was educated in Copenhagen. After the War he returned
to Berlin and, as before stated, resided at Bleichroederstrasse
31A, Berlin-Pankow. In 1925 he is known to have had
communist tendencies, and an important communist leader was
arrested in his flat in Berlin. In the following year he
was Trade Union Chairman in the district directorate of the
Revolutionary Trades Union Opposition and was also district
leader of the Red Front Fighters Union. In 1928 he became
a member of the Provincial Committee of Unemployed for Greater
Berlin and was at the same time holding an official post in
the Building Trade Section of the Communist Industrial Union.
While in Berlin he was in possession of passports No. 168,
dated 26.9.27, and No. 243, dated 12.5.32, the number of the
latter passport, it should be noted, does not agree with
the one given by the Shanghai passport authorities although
the date of issue is identical. His wife is in possession
of passport No. 170/29, dated 8.8.29.

19th December, 1935.

PERSONAL & SECRET.

My dear Givens,

With reference to our telephone conversation
this morning, I send you herewith copy of a report which
has been received on the subject of WILHELM WLOCH, who
was connected with the "Rose York" case.

It was he who financed Dubovsky as a dentist,
and, while the latter's name is unknown in Germany, it
is interesting to note that the Berlin Directories of 1933
and 1934-35 show a man called Rudolf Rugowsky living in
the same block of flats at Bleichroederstrasse 31 a as
Wloch. It is possible that Dubovsky is a false name
suggested by Rugowsky.

You are of course at liberty to make any use
you like of this information, but I should be grateful
if you do not disclose the source from which you obtained
it.

Yours sincerely,
〔签名〕

（批：S2. For attention. Please ascertain present address of Wloch. JAG/）

T. P. Givens, Esq.

（右上角手写注记：D.S. Nauckman OAR. 19/12）

Date October 9, 1935.

Subject Wloch and the First Dental Clinic.

Made by D.P.S. Henchman. Forwarded by D S J Boyce

Further to my report dated 27th August, 1935 and
with reference to the Dental Clinic situated on the 2nd floor
of No.542 Avenue Joffre, I have to state that this Dental Clinic
is owned by W. Wloch who employs Doubovsky to supervise and
direct the concern.
Wilhelm Wloch is a German who is not registered at
the German Consulate. Examination of his landing papers shows
that he was born in Berlin and that his home address is Berlin -
Pankow, Bleichroderstrasse 31A. His occupation is given as
that of merchant. His passport, No.47 Berlin - Gruenau, was
issued on the 12th May 1932 and was visaed on 11th August 1934
at Copenhagen. He travelled from Copenhagen to Marseilles
and from there on the M. M. Co.'s vessel "Porthos" to Shanghai
where he arrived on 12th October 1934.
From 8th November 1934 he resided at Flat 62, No.233
Race Course Road, this flat he rented on a monthly basis. Towards
the end of last year, probably late in December, he opened
the First Dental Clinic at 542 Avenue Joffre and, as previously
stated, appointed Dr. W. Doubovsky as director. It is reported
that Wloch has already spent over $8,000 in this enterprise and
although at one time it prospered business at the present time
is very slack.
On 31st August Wloch moved from his Race Course Road
address and took up residence at a boarding house known as
"Lowlands" 365 Route Cardinal Mercier, his only baggage was a
small leather trunk.
Besides Doubovsky there are six members on the staff
of the Dental Clinic, these are as follows:-
V.I. Valegjanin, Dentist.

继我于1935年8月27日的报告之后，并关于位于霞飞路542号二楼的牙科诊所，兹陈述如下：该牙科诊所由 W. Wloch 所有，其雇佣 Doubovsky 负责监督和指导该机构。
Wilhelm Wloch 是一名德国人，未在德国领事馆注册。对其登陆证件的审查显示，他出生于柏林，家庭住址为柏林-潘科夫（Berlin-Pankow），Bleichroderstrasse 31A。其职业登记为商人。他的护照，编号47 Berlin - Gruenau，签发于1932年5月12日，并于1934年8月11日在哥本哈根获得签证。他从哥本哈根前往马赛，并从那里乘坐法国邮船公司（M. M. Co.）的“波尔多斯”号（Porthos）轮船抵达上海，到达日期为1934年10月12日。
自1934年11月8日起，他居住在跑马厅路233号62室公寓，该公寓系按月租赁。去年年底，大概是12月下旬，他在霞飞路542号开设了第一牙科诊所，如前所述，任命 W. Doubovsky 博士为主任。据报，Wloch 在此项事业上已花费超过8,000元，虽然曾一度繁荣，但目前业务非常清淡。
8月31日，Wloch 搬离了其在跑马厅路的住所，入住位于麦尔西爱路365号、名为“Lowlands”的寄宿公寓，其随身行李仅有一个小皮箱。
除 Doubovsky 外，牙科诊所还有六名职员，名单如下：-
V.I. Valegjanin，牙医。

Made by D.P.S. Henchman. Forwarded by D.S.I. Royal.

In connection with the movements of the above mentioned
woman I have to state that Mrs. Rosa York of 69 St. Charles
Square, London, W.1, suspected Communist agent, arrived in
Shanghai on 3.8.35. She travelled from Trieste on the
Lloyd Triestino liner "Conte Verde" in which vessel she was
a 2nd class passenger and occupied cabin No. 18. Her pass-
port No. 316721, issued on 5.4.35, which among other places
is visaed for U.S.S.R., states that she is the wife of
Maurice Samuel York formerly known as Yedvop and that she was
born in London on 10.12.03. Her occupation is given as
that of secretary. Visas in the passport indicate that since
April 5, 1935, Mrs. York has travelled in Finland, Poland,
Latvia, Austria, Lithuania and Germany and it has been
ascertained that her passage to China was booked in Vienna;
most of her travelling in Europe seems to have been done by
air. Mrs. York previously travelled on Foreign Office
passport 6A9221/1928, which has since been cancelled.

Mrs. York is of a slightly Jewish appearance, about
5 feet and 3 inches in height, eyes blue, prominent large nose,
hair brown. She stoops slightly and is inclined to stoutness.
She dresses simply and in typically English bourgeois style.
She appears to be fond of art and apparently has read widely
though it is very difficult to get her to express her views
about anything of a controversial nature and she refuses to
discuss politics in any shape or form. She has a knowledge
of languages and speaks French, German and possibly Norwegian.

On the 25th August Mrs. York went to the American Express
Company, Kiangse Road, and booked her passage home to
England. She made reservations on the Empress of Russia
sailing on 25th August. From Vancouver she will travel via
Chicago to New York and from thence to Plymouth arriving on
the 22nd Sept. She stated to the clerk in the American
Express Co. that she wanted to get home as soon as possible,
this was at variance to the wish which she had expressed to
the undersigned to whom she had mentioned her intention of
staying in Japan for at least a fortnight.

On the 21st August Mrs. York went to Hangchow. She was
followed to the North Station and was seen to leave on the
3.15 p.m. train. No one met her at the station. After a
brief visit Mrs. York returned to Shanghai on the 25th Aug.
She went to the Burlington Hotel picked up the luggage she
had left there and then drove to the Shanghai and Hongkew
Wharf where she boarded the Empress of Russia at 4.30 p.m.
and occupied Cabin No. 207. The Empress of Russia sailed
at 6.30 p.m. and between that time and her arrival at the
North Station from Hangchow Mrs. York had made no contact
with any of her friends.
